summary: The new regime is the default. You must opt for the old regime if you want it.
Salaried employees get a standard deduction of Rs 75,000.
Salaried employees get a standard deduction of Rs 50,000.
Rebate up to Rs 60,000 if taxable income is up to Rs 12 lakh. Salary up to Rs 12.75 lakh pays no tax.
Rebate up to Rs 12,500 if taxable income is up to Rs 5 lakh.
Deduction up to Rs 1.5 lakh for PPF, ELSS, LIC and similar. Only in the old regime.
Deduction for health insurance premium. Only in the old regime.
House rent allowance exemption is available only in the old regime.
For salary income, one house property and interest income, with total income up to Rs 50 lakh.
Consider ITR-2 if you have capital gains from shares or mutual funds along with salary.
For business or freelance income, consider ITR-3 or ITR-4.
A 4% cess is added on the tax amount.
Your employer deducts TDS and gives you Form 16. Use it while filing your ITR.
E-verify your return within 30 days of filing, otherwise it is treated as invalid.
